value.body: An industrial engineer studies how people, machines and materials come together and finds ways to make work faster, safer and cheaper. Employers include manufacturers (automotive, apparel, electronics, consumer goods), warehouses, logistics firms and hospitals. A typical day includes time studies on the floor, analysing data and running improvement projects with production teams.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, time-study methods, lean tools (5S, value-stream mapping), simulation

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join manufacturing or logistics firms as graduate engineer trainees in the industrial engineering or operations team. Lean or Six Sigma training and a shop-floor internship help.

value.title: At a glance
items: The role sits between engineering and management.
It often leads to operations or supply-chain roles.
Next roles: senior industrial engineer, operations manager, continuous-improvement lead.
